messages.author: cb810af641e6cd25
messages.subject: MSstatsPTM yielded non-existent PTMs.
parts:
Hello,
         I search my TimsTOF DDA data by MaxQuant 2.1.0.0, and then processed output "evidence.txt" with MSstatsPTM, and it seems everything is OK. 
But in those processed data, I found that it created some ridiculous PTMs as those PTMs should not exist in my database.

For example, 
P49450_S17_S33, P15924_S165_S180, Q8NDI1_S171_S188, P38919_S37, P50402_S33, those sites do not exist, but after processing they are created.

The 33rd amino acid of P50402 is L but S 
>sp|P50402|EMD_HUMAN Emerin OS=Homo sapiens OX=9606 GN=EMD PE=1 SV=1 MDNYADLSDTELTTLLRRYNIPHGPVVGSTRRLYEKKIFEYETQRRRLSPPSSSAASSYS FSDLNSTRGDADMYDLPKKEDALLYQSKGYNDDYYEESYFTTRTYGEPESAGPSRAVRQS VTSFPDADAFHHQVHDDDLLSSSEEECKDRERPMYGRDSAYQSITHYRPVSASRSSLDLS YYPTSSSTSFMSSSSSSSSWLTRRAIRPENRAPGAGLGQDRQVPLWGQLLLFLVFVIVLF FIYHFMQAEEGNPF

MaxQuant output, selfmade annotation, database and MSstatsPTM processed data were shared via Google cloud drive.
(the format of column "Proteins" did not suit for processing so I corrected to "UNIPROT ID")

Bellow area my processing lines in R.
rm(list = ls())
library(MSstats)
library(MSstatsPTM)
setwd("E:/source_document")
maxq_lf_annotation <- read.csv("maxQ_annotation.csv")
maxq_lf_evidence <- read.delim("evidence.txt")

msstats_format_lf <- MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat(evidence = maxq_lf_evidence,
                                           annotation = maxq_lf_annotation,
                                           fasta_path = "E:/source_document/homo.fasta",
                                           fasta_protein_name = "uniprot_ac",
                                           mod_id = "\\(Phospho \\(STY\\)\\)",
                                           use_unmod_peptides = TRUE,
                                           labeling_type = "LF",
                                           which_proteinid_ptm = "Proteins")

MSstatsPTM.summary = dataSummarizationPTM(msstats_format_lf, verbose = FALSE,
                                          use_log_file = FALSE, append = FALSE)

PTM_data <- MSstatsPTM.summary$PTM$ProteinLevelData
colnames(PTM_data)

library(tidyr)
x1 <- PTM_data[,c(2:3,6)]
x2 <- x1 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = SUBJECT, values_from = LogIntensities)
write.csv(x2,file = "phosph_data.csv")

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM yielded non-existent PTMs.
parts:
Hello,

Thank you for pointing out this bug. This was a specific problem for the MaxQ converter when there were multiple modifications. I have pushed a bug fix that will be available on Bioconductor tomorrow (around noon EST). If you want to use the newest version of the package before then you can download it straight from Github.

I added a new parameter to this converter called `remove_other_mods`. This will give you the ability to keep or remove peptides with modifications that are not of interest (e.g. (Acetyl (Protein N-term))AAAAPDSRVS(Phospho (STY))EEENLK).

Devon
